title: telemetry-driven-prefill-defaults-and-compact-quant-reconciler
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Introduces telemetry-driven defaults for prefill/batching and a compact quantization reconciler to synthesise safe per-tenant quant hints. Improves unit economics without changing public API.
description:
Context and motivation: We frequently see tenants with similar traffic shapes receiving suboptimal defaults for prefill, batching, and quantization. Manual tuning is slow and error-prone. This PR wires observed serving telemetry into a small, deterministic heuristic pipeline that generates tenant-level 'prefill defaults' and a compact quant-reconciler that synthesizes a small set of safe quantization hints for downstream rollout. The goal is to reduce per-token cost by enabling better batching/prefill and safer quant suggestions while preserving latency SLOs and output quality.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a telemetry consumer that computes workload fingerprints (sequence length distribution, inter-arrival times, KV reuse score) and stores a condensed profile in tenant metadata.
- Implements a Prefill Defaults generator: maps workload fingerprints to prefill/batching/caching defaults (prefill_enabled, prefill_size_hint, batch_shape_hint, kv_cache_ttl_hint). Defaults are conservative and include safe fallbacks.
- Adds Compact Quant Reconciler: a lightweight synthesizer that proposes 2-3 quant profiles per tenant (e.g., fp16, int8-q4, int8-q4+KV), with a priority score and rollback safety thresholds; output is packaged as a suggestion payload for the Optimize service.
- Exposes a dry-run API endpoint and CLI dry-run helper so operators can simulate outcomes against historical traces.
- Telemetry and config changes are opt-in via tenant flags; default behavior for existing tenants unchanged.

- b5e9a21: defaults: implement prefill defaults generator and mapping table
- c2d7f90: reconcile: compact quant reconciler synthesizer + scoring heuristics

Design notes and safety:
- All generated suggestions are advisory; application of defaults requires explicit tenant opt-in via tenant flags. That reduces blast radius.
- The reconciler includes a 'quality delta check' that tags suggestions as 'safe' only if historical traces show <=1% expected token-quality divergence (heuristic based on decoding score proxies).
- We limit suggested quant profiles to at most 3 variants and include a rollback TTL that auto-reverts suggestions if telemetry indicates degradation.

Review conversation (high level excerpts):
- Marco Li (reviewer): "Nice end-to-end. Two asks: (1) can we expose the scoring curve for debugging in the UI? (2) tighten the unit test for fallback when telemetry is sparse."
- Author (Aisha): "Added a debug-score endpoint and added an integration test that simulates sparse telemetry and verifies conservative fallback (see tests/integration/test_prefill_quant_reconciler.py)."
- Evelyn Chen: "Concern about KV cache TTL interactions with dedicated capacity—can caching hints cause unintended memory pressure?"
- Author: "We limit KV cache TTL to tenant quotas and surface a warning if suggested TTL would exceed current quota. Also added a check in defaults_generator to clamp TTL to tenant configuration."
- Samir Patel: "CI flaky test on GPU CI failing on int8 emulation."
- Author: "Fixed by moving int8 emulation setup into test fixture and added retry for the GPU job; re-ran CI."

CI summary: initial run: 2 failures (integration/gpu-int8-emulation flake, lint warning). Fixes landed in c2d7f90 and 1e3b4f2. Final CI: all checks passed. Checks include: unit-tests, integration-tests (cpu), integration-tests (gpu-emulation), lint, mypy, e2e-dryrun.

Operational notes and rollout plan:
- Feature is behind tenant flag (opt-in) and feature-gate at the service layer. Default for all tenants remains unchanged.
- Ops runbook included in docs/runbooks/telemetry-prefill-quant.md describing how to simulate, evaluate expected cost delta, and opt-in a tenant to suggestions.
- We ran a 48-hour dry-run on three internal tenants and observed a mean per-token cost delta of -12% with median latency +1.3ms (within SLO). Those findings are summarized in the runbook.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-25 after approvals from Marco and Evelyn. Release notes added to the changelog.
